To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Sus4 gene fragment studied contains several types of sequences, each type being characteristic of some potato cultivars; (2) these types of sequences are different from one another by the presence of a mononucleotide repeat (T)8 and by an insertion in intron 4 and intron 5; (3) these sequence types differ from one another by several nucleotide substitutions and indels; (4) these sequence types are characterized by specific amino acid substitutions;
we identified four types of Sus4 gene sequences, and revealed 16 amino acid substitutions, which were specific for some cultivars.
the Sus4 gene of potato cultivars has intraspecific variability and that specific nucleotide and aminoacid substitutions are cultivar-specific.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of intraspecific genetic variability of the Sus4 sucrose synthase-encoding gene in potato cultivars.
the identification of intraspecific variation of the sucrose gene Sus4 in potato cultivars and the search for the associations between this variation and the starch content in potato tubers.
identification and characterization of the Sus4 intraspecific variability in potato and the search for associations of the Sus4 mutational changes and starch content in tuber.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the variability of Sus4 gene is not associated with the variability of starch content in potato tubers.
the intraspecific variability in the Sus4 gene of the potato cultivars is low and is not associated with starch content.
the variability of the Sus4 sequence is not related to the starch content in the potato tubers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Sus4 gene is polymorphic in potato and that the polymorphic sites are not associated with the starch content.
we have identified a number of SNPs that are cultivar specific, and these can be used in the future as markers for identifying potato cultivar.
the intraspecific variability and the polymorphism in the Sus4 gene of potato are high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Sus4 gene is highly variable in potato cultivars.
the Sus4 gene is highly variable and can be used as a marker for identifying potato cultivar/genotype.
the intraspecific variability is high in the potato Sus4 gene, which makes this gene a promising candidate for the identification of potato cultivars and genotypes.
